title: When Does Restarting a Search Help Once Restart Time Is Charged? Exact Finite Random-Walk Tests
target_platform: Python standard-library Fraction arithmetic; finite nearest-neighbor Markov walk with absorbing 0 and reflecting L
interest_statement: Richard authorized a separate inquiry on any topic after MISSION-062 full closeout. I chose the tension between abandoning a long search to improve its average and paying real time to restart. The interesting gap is whether a two-moment local condition actually classifies finite-rate improvement, and how clock conventions move the boundary. This is a bounded exploration of known restart physics, not a novelty claim.
hypothesis: For every L=9..32 and start x=1..L in an unbiased nearest-neighbor walk on 0..L (0 absorbing; L deterministically steps to L-1), and every frozen reset-cost c in C(L,x)={0,1,2,4,8,max(c_star-1/2,0),max(c_star,0),max(c_star+1/2,0)}, the exact moment condition Var(T)>E[T]^2+(2c-1)E[T] is equivalent to the existence of a strict reduction in expected absorption time for at least one reset probability in R={2^-j:j=1..24} union {3/4,7/8}. Here c_star=1+E[T(T-1)]/(2E[T])-E[T]. At each event, reset to x with probability r and spend c time units, or take a walk step with probability 1-r and spend one time unit. No walk step occurs on reset. Equality predicts no strict grid improvement.
falsification_criteria: FALSIFIED if any registered held-out (L,x,c) disagrees between the moment prediction and exact sampled-rate search, after reproducing the disagreeing case with an independent dense rational Markov linear solver. Any validity-gate mismatch, resource breach, missing registered cases, or inability to independently confirm a counterexample leaves UNASSESSED with verdict null. A corroboration applies only to this finite family, cost construction and probability grid, not to all rates, arbitrary graphs, continuous diffusion or real search systems.
baseline_evidence: Primary literature establishes restart as a first-passage framework and a sufficient infinitesimal geometric-restart criterion. Bonomo/Pal 2102.00895, Eq25, reports CV^2>1-1/mean for its timing convention and studies two absorbing boundaries. Our reflecting boundary and explicit total reset cost are specified separately. The generalization from a local derivative to finite-grid existence is the hypothesis under test, not a theorem borrowed from the paper. No held-out L>=9 calculation has been run.
experiment: Register PROPOSED with reciprocal soft link to MISSION-063 and compile indexes. Develop an exact tridiagonal discounted-survival solver and a structurally independent dense rational Markov solver; validate only on L<=8. Then commit protocol.md, freeze.json and code hashes in a separate command before any L>=9 computation. Held-out primary L9..32, all starts, exact cost and rate sets above. Independent gate includes 48 prespecified held-out dense checks at L9,16,24,32; starts1,ceil(L/2),L; costs0,2; rates1/2,1/16. All comparisons exact Fraction; no Monte Carlo or floating tolerance. Stop at first independently confirmed counterexample or full completion. Raw comparisons, best grid rate/mean and resource evidence retained.

lessons_learned: Charging a full time unit per reset shifts the local variance condition from CV²>1-1/mu to CV²>1+1/mu in the stated model.
The local moment rule classified the tested reflected-walk grid, but an independently checked post-hoc bimodal example shows no universal local-to-global implication.
Separate finite exact evidence, continuous-rate claims and practical retry analogies; retain clock convention and overhead.
